passages.text: At dawn, when Peter came forward to converse, Simon spoke first: “As I left yesterday, I promised you that today I would return, debate with you, and show that the one who fashioned the world is not the highest God, but another, who alone is good and has remained unknown until now. To begin, then: do you say that the maker himself is also lawgiver, or not? If he is lawgiver, he is just; and being just, he is not good. If he is not good, Jesus proclaimed another when he said, ‘Do not call me good, for the good one is one, the Father in the heavens.’ This does not agree with the lawgiver’s being both just and good.” Peter said, “First tell us: on account of what actions does the good one seem to you good, and on account of what actions the just one just? In this way we can aim our arguments at the target.” Simon said, “You tell me first: what do you think goodness is? Or justice, too?”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δίκαιος δὲ ὢν ἀγαθὸς οὐκ ἔστιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: being just, he is not good
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Simon’s opposition of justice and goodness as his claim, not the translator’s conclusion.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κατὰ σκοποῦ τοὺς λόγους πέμπωμεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: aim our arguments at the target
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the aiming/target image.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Σὺ πρῶτον εἰπὲ τί σοι δοκεῖ τὸ ἀγαθόν; ἢ καὶ τὸ δίκαιον;
lexical_decisions.chosen: You tell me first: what do you think goodness is? Or justice, too?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantival good and just are rendered as goodness and justice. Or ... too preserves the second question’s disjunctive and additive ἢ καί rather than replacing both questions with one and-linked list.

passages.text: Peter said, “So that I do not spend time in a more contentious debate, rightly demanding that you answer my questions, I will give the answers as you wish, although I was the one who asked. I say that the good person is the one who provides, as I see the maker himself doing when he provides the sun to good and evil people and rain to the righteous and unrighteous.” Simon said, “This is most unjust: he provides the same things to the righteous and unrighteous.” Peter said, “Then you tell us from now on how he would act to be good.” Simon said, “You must say.” Peter said, “I will. If, by providing the same things to the good and righteous and also to the evil and unrighteous, he is according to you not even just, and if, by providing good things to the good and bad things to the bad, you would reasonably call him just, what further course of action could he take, if not this way: providing temporary things to the evil, in case they change, and eternal things to the good, provided they remain? Thus, in providing for all but granting favors to different recipients, his justice is good and all the more patient in this respect, if he forgives the sins of sinners who reorient and also promises eternal life to those who have acted well. But in judging at the end and assigning to each what is deserved, he is just. If, then, these matters rightly stand this way, acknowledge it; but if they do not seem right to you, refute them.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν παρεκτικόν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the one who provides
lexical_decisions.rationale: Goodness is defined through giving/provision in this argument; generous is an alternative, but provision is kept explicit.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἁμαρτωλοῖς μὲν μετανοοῦσιν χαρίζεται τὰ ἁμαρτήματα
lexical_decisions.chosen: he forgives the sins of sinners who reorient
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses POB reorientation wording, traditionally repent, preserving forgiveness and its relation to the response. Who reorient renders the participle; the encompassing if is separately retained for the printed εἰ.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ζωὴν αἰώνιον ὑπογράφει
lexical_decisions.chosen: promises eternal life
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑπογράφω can pledge, prescribe, or outline. Promises fits the positive undertaking to those who act well, without claiming automatic possession already.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς σοὶ δοκεῖ αὐτὸς ὢν ἐπυθόμην ποιήσομαι τὰς· ἀποκρίσεις.
lexical_decisions.chosen: I will give the answers as you wish, although I was the one who asked.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied construction juxtaposes participial ὢν with finite ἐπυθόμην irregularly. The English reads this contextually as Peter answering despite having himself asked. A relative ὃς in place of printed ὢν would support a smoother clause but would be conjectural; it is not substituted. The supplied stop between article and noun in τὰς· ἀποκρίσεις is a print punctuation feature, not an alleged OCR defect.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ μὲν πᾶσιν παρέχειν, διαφόροις δὲ χαρίζεσθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: in providing for all but granting favors to different recipients
lexical_decisions.rationale: διαφόροις is taken as a dative of recipients, contrasting everyone with differentiated beneficiaries. It can also mean distinguished or worthy recipients; the main text leaves the difference unspecified. The previous different-gifts rendering would require an instrumental interpretation, by differing gifts, rather than an accusative object; that is a material alternative but the recipient reading is more direct with χαρίζεσθαι.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ μακρόθυμον ταύτη μᾶλλον, εἰ ἁμαρτωλοῖς μὲν μετανοοῦσιν χαρίζεται τὰ ἁμαρτήματα, εὖ πράξασιν δὲ καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον ὑπογράφει.
lexical_decisions.chosen: and all the more patient in this respect, if he forgives the sins of sinners who reorient and also promises eternal life to those who have acted well.
lexical_decisions.rationale: If preserves εἰ governing the argument through both forgiveness and the promise of life. The participle who reorient is distinct from that condition; the sentence is not changed into an unconditional assertion by a colon.

passages.text: Simon said, “How, then, when the maker was known—the one who formed Adam and was known to the righteous according to the law, and furthermore to the righteous and unrighteous and the whole world—does your teacher, coming after all those people, say, ‘No one knew the Father except the Son, just as no one knows the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him’? He would not have said these things unless he were announcing a certain Father who is in secrecy, whom the law also calls Most High, from whom no good or evil utterance has been heard, as Jeremiah too testifies in the Lamentations. In accordance with the number of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt, who are seventy, and marking out the nations’ boundaries by seventy languages, this one gave the Hebrews as a portion to his Son, who is also called Lord and ordered heaven and earth, and appointed him God of gods. By gods I mean those who have received the other portions of the nations. Laws therefore issued from all the gods just mentioned to their own portions, namely the remaining nations; likewise the law established among the Hebrews issued from the Son, the Lord of all. It was determined to be this way so that if someone takes refuge in someone’s law, he becomes part of the portion of the one whose law he has undertaken to practice. No one knew the Most High Father who is in secrecy, just as no one knew of this one’s Son that he is Son. Indeed, you, assigning to the Son the distinctive attributes of the secret Most High, do not know that he is Son, being Father of the Jesus whom you call Messiah.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν ἀπορρήτοις
lexical_decisions.chosen: in secrecy
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expression can mean among unrevealed mysteries or in the secret realm. In secrecy preserves the hidden status without inventing a named location.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κατὰ ἀριθμὸν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ
lexical_decisions.chosen: In accordance with the number of the sons of Israel
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Israel, not another textual witness’s sons of God or angels; the explicit count seventy remains.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ αὐτοῦ υἱῷ τῷ καὶ „κυρίῳ“ λεγομένῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: to his Son, who is also called Lord
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains Simon’s distinction between the Most High and his Son, who is the maker in this proposal, not the translator’s own theological identification.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ καθ’ ὑμᾶς λεγομένου χριστοῦ
lexical_decisions.chosen: the Jesus whom you call Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: χριστός is a disputed independent title attributed by Simon to the other party’s Jesus, so Messiah preserves the title’s force.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅστις κατὰ ἀριθμὸν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, οἳ εἰσῆλθον εἰς Αἴγυπτον (οἵ εἰσιν ἑβδομήκοντα), καὶ πρὸς τὰ ὅρια τῶν ἐθνῶν περιγράψας γλώσσαις ἑβδομήκοντα
lexical_decisions.chosen: In accordance with the number of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt, who are seventy, and marking out the nations’ boundaries by seventy languages
lexical_decisions.rationale: The object of περιγράψας is implicit. The English takes the boundaries named in πρὸς τὰ ὅρια as the contextual object of marking out, not as a direct Greek accusative object outside the preposition. A more formally separated alternative is having marked out divisions by seventy languages in accordance with that number and in relation to the nations’ boundaries. Both number and boundary expressions constrain the delineation; no additional printed noun is claimed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀπὸ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ πάντων κυρίου
lexical_decisions.chosen: from the Son, the Lord of all
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes the second genitive phrase appositionally, since the Son was already explicitly called Lord in this proposal. From the Son of the Lord of all is a material alternative attaching the second genitive as the Son’s parent; the main text does not claim the appositional grouping is uniquely settled.

passages.text: After Simon said these things, Peter said to him, “Can you call that very one to witness that you believe this—not the one you now say is in secrecy, but the one you believe in without acknowledging him? For you talk nonsense by defining one thing in place of another. Therefore, if you call him to witness that you believe what you say, I will answer you; but if you stand debating with me things you do not believe, you force me to strike at emptiness.” Simon said, “I heard from one of your disciples ....” Peter said, “Do not bear false witness.” Simon said, “Do not abuse me, you utterly rash man.” Peter said, “Until you name the person who said it, you are a liar.” Simon said, “Suppose that I invented these things, or even heard them from someone else: answer me about them. For if they cannot be overturned, I have learned that this is the truth.” Peter said, “If it is a human fabrication, I will not answer it. But if you have been gripped by the supposition that it is true, acknowledge this very thing to me, and I myself also have something to say about it.” Simon said, “Once for all, I think it is so. If you have anything to say about these things, answer.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: διαμαρτύρασθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: call ... to witness
lexical_decisions.rationale: The demand invokes the one actually believed in as witness, not a request for a merely informal reassurance.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κατὰ κενοῦ με παίειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: strike at emptiness
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the striking-at-a-void metaphor.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Παρὰ τινὸς τῶν σῶν μαθητῶν ἀκήκοα . . . .
lexical_decisions.chosen: I heard from one of your disciples ....
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly four dots remain for the printed gap; the alleged disclosure’s missing content is not restored.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ δὲ ὑπονοίᾳ αὐτοῦ κεχράτησαι ὡς ἀληθοῦς
lexical_decisions.chosen: But if you have been gripped by the supposition that it is true
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected reading has κεχράτησαι, interpreted contextually as passive holding or gripping. Regular κεκράτησαι is only a possible spelling regularization, not substituted or described as verified text. The English clarifies that the supposition concerns the account’s truth, while preserving the printed construction and its uncertainty.

source_issues.source_quote: Παρὰ τινὸς τῶν σῶν μαθητῶν ἀκήκοα . . . .
source_issues.issue: Exactly four printed dots remain; the missing report is not reconstructed.

passages.text: Peter said, “If this is so, you act with the greatest impiety. For if it belongs to the Son who ordered heaven and earth to reveal his Father who is in secret to whomever he wishes, you, as I said, act with the greatest impiety by revealing to those to whom he did not reveal.” Simon said, “But he himself wants me to reveal.” Peter said, “You do not understand what I say, Simon. Yet listen and understand. Saying, ‘To those to whom the Son wishes he will reveal,’ does not mean that someone learns such a thing by teaching, but only by revelation. Revelation is what lies secretly in all human hearts, covered, being uncovered without a voice expressing his will. Thus one comes to know not by being taught, but by understanding. Yet the one who has understood is not permitted to demonstrate this to another, since he himself was not taught; nor can he reveal it, since he himself is not the Son—unless he says that he himself is the Son. But you are not the standing Son. For if you were Son, you would certainly know those worthy of such revelation. But you do not know. For if you knew, you would do the things done by those who know.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἄνευ φωνῆς τῆς αὐτοῦ βουλῆς ἀποκαλυπτόμενον
lexical_decisions.chosen: being uncovered without a voice expressing his will
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive τῆς αὐτοῦ βουλῆς is attached to voice, a voice of his will, expressed readably as a voice expressing his will. It is not assigned independent instrumental force as by his will, for which the supplied genitive gives no established grammatical support. Nonvocal disclosure remains explicit.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ ἑστὼς υἱός
lexical_decisions.chosen: the standing Son
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the standing epithet and Son together, rather than replacing them with a later named title or deleting the unusual description.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν ἐν ἀπορρήτοις αὐτοῦ πατέρα
lexical_decisions.chosen: his Father who is in secret
lexical_decisions.rationale: The secrecy phrase is attributive inside the Father noun phrase, not the manner in which the Son reveals him. Who is in secret makes this attachment explicit without specifying a named hidden realm.

passages.text: Simon said, “I admit I did not understand how you mean, ‘You would do the things done by those who know.’” Peter said, “If you did not understand, you also cannot know each person’s mind. And if you do not know, you also do not know those worthy of revelation. If you do not know, you are not Son; but the Son knows, and therefore reveals to those he wishes as being worthy.” Simon said, “Let me not deceive: I know those who are worthy, and I am not Son. Yet I did not understand what this is, ‘He reveals to those he wishes,’ as you say. I said that I did not understand not because I did not know, but because I knew that those present did not understand, so that you would state it more clearly and those for whose sake we also conduct the discussion might understand.” Peter said, “I cannot state it more clearly. Since you have understood it, explain it yourself.” Simon said, “I am not obliged to state your views.” Peter said, “It seems to me, Simon, that you do not understand it and are unwilling to admit it, lest, being caught in ignorance, you be exposed as not being the standing Son. For this is what you hint at, even if you do not wish to say it plainly. Thus I know your intentions from your hints, being a disciple of a true prophet, not a prophet. But you, though you do not understand even what is plainly said, wish to call yourself Son, standing against us.” Simon said, “I will remove every excuse from you. I admit that I did not understand what this is: ‘And to those to whom the Son wishes, he reveals.’ So state it more clearly.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ ἑστὼς υἱός
lexical_decisions.chosen: the standing Son
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the epithet tied to Simon’s alleged claim; it is not identified with an external historical person.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: προφήτου ἀληθοῦς μαθητὴς ὤν, οὐ προφήτης
lexical_decisions.chosen: being a disciple of a true prophet, not a prophet
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Peter’s explicit denial of being a prophet in this statement, rather than harmonizing it to a later title.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Μὴ ἀπατῶ·
lexical_decisions.chosen: Let me not deceive:
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀπατῶ is first-person singular, compatible with a first-person subjunctive here; let me not deceive preserves that person and the negative. The possible interrogative indicative alternative is Am I deceiving?, expecting a negative answer. The edition’s printed stop fits the chosen noninterrogative construction, but does not settle the form’s mood. No second-person imperative or replacement Greek is introduced.

passages.text: After Peter said this, praise arose from the crowds. Simon, thoroughly exposed, blushed in shame, rubbed his forehead, and said, “But they call me a magician, defeated by Peter, and also caught in argument. Yet if someone is caught in argument and taken unawares, he does not thereby have the truth within him defeated; for the weakness of its defender is not the truth of the defeated party. Nevertheless I tell you that I judged everyone present worthy to know the Father who is in secret. Therefore, when I reveal him to them publicly, they should not be angry with me out of envy, since I wish to do them good.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: συλλογιζόμενον
lexical_decisions.chosen: caught in argument
lexical_decisions.rationale: The form can mean reasoning or being brought under a syllogistic argument. The context of defeat and being taken unawares favors being caught in argument; reasoning is a material alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ ἡ ἀσθένεια τοῦ ἐκδικοῦντος ἀλήθειά ἐστιν τοῦ νικωμένου
lexical_decisions.chosen: the weakness of its defender is not the truth of the defeated party
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the compact distinction between a weak defender and the truth he defends rather than rewriting it as truth’s weakness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ αὐτοῖς διὰ φθόνον ἐμοὶ τῷ εὐεργετεῖν αὐτοὺς θέλοντι χαλεπαίνειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: they should not be angry with me out of envy, since I wish to do them good
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes αὐτοῖς as the persons for whom getting angry is inappropriate, leaving the grammatical third-person reference intact instead of silently changing it to you, Peter.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: γνῶναι τὸν ἐν ἀπορρήτοις πατέρα
lexical_decisions.chosen: to know the Father who is in secret
lexical_decisions.rationale: The secrecy phrase describes the Father, not a secret manner of knowing. This distinction fits Simon’s immediately following public disclosure and agrees with the attributive rendering in 18.6.

passages.text: Peter said, “Since you have spoken in this way to please the crowds present, I will speak not to please them, but truthfully. Tell me: how do you know that everyone present is worthy, when not even one agreed with you as you disclosed it? For their praising me against you is not the act of people agreeing with you, but with me, to whom they also assigned praise as someone who had spoken rightly. But since God, being just, judges each person’s mind—which you say is true—he would not have wished this to be given to those on the right through the left. By the same reasoning, someone who receives anything from a thief is himself liable. Therefore, for this reason, he did not wish them to receive what you bring, but rather through the Son appointed to reveal. For who can reasonably reveal the Father except the Son alone, since he knows who is worthy of such revelation? Thus this cannot be taught or learned by teaching, but must be revealed by an inexpressible hand to the one worthy to know it.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: διὰ τῆς ἀριστερᾶς τοῖς δεξιοῖς
lexical_decisions.chosen: to those on the right through the left
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the right/left opposition without identifying unprinted named camps or persons.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀφράστῳ χειρὶ
lexical_decisions.chosen: by an inexpressible hand
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the hand image, not merely a generic divine act.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τίνι γὰρ εὔλογόν ἐστιν ἀποκαλύπτειν τὸν πατέρα ἢ υἱῷ μόνῳ διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι τῆς τοιαύτης ἀποκαλύψεως τὸν ἄξιον;
lexical_decisions.chosen: For who can reasonably reveal the Father except the Son alone, since he knows who is worthy of such revelation?
lexical_decisions.rationale: τίνι and υἱῷ identify the person for whom revealing is appropriate, thus the revealer. The Son’s preceding appointment and knowledge of worthy recipients confirm this role. The English does not make him the recipient by saying to whom the Father is revealed.

passages.text: “We, Simon, do not say that two angels were sent from the great power, also called the sovereign power, one to create a world and the other to lay down the law. Nor do we say that each came to the things he had made and announced himself as their original author. Nor do we speak of the standing one who will stand as an adversary. Learn how you disbelieve even this hypothesis. The power you say is in secrecy is full of ignorance, for it did not foreknow the ingratitude of the angels it sent.” While Peter was saying this, Simon became very angry and interrupted him, saying, “Why do you babble, you bold man, most reckless of all, plainly disclosing the secrets before uninstructed crowds?” Peter said, “Why do you begrudge the benefit given to the hearers present?” Simon said, “Then do you acknowledge that such knowledge is a benefit?” Peter said, “I do: for once falsehood is known, it gives the benefit of not falling into it through ignorance.” Simon said, “It seems to me that you cannot answer what I put before you. I mean that your teacher too says that there is a certain Father in secrecy.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς μεγάλης δυνάμεως, ἔτι τε καὶ τῆς κυρίας λεγομένης
lexical_decisions.chosen: the great power, also called the sovereign power
lexical_decisions.rationale: κυρίας can qualify power as sovereign, ruling, or mistress-like; sovereign power gives its authority sense without adding a separate named deity.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδὲ ὁ ἑστὼς στησόμενος ἀντικείμενος.
lexical_decisions.chosen: Nor do we speak of the standing one who will stand as an adversary.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The nominal clause is extremely compressed. The main rendering carries do we speak from the preceding repeated denial and preserves standing, future standing, and adversary without supplying a named identity. Nor is the standing one going to stand as an adversary is another possible grouping.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀτέχνως τὰ ἀπόρρητα
lexical_decisions.chosen: plainly disclosing the secrets
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀτέχνως here means plainly or without qualification, not necessarily in an unskilled manner.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τολμηρὲ καὶ πάντων προπετέστατε
lexical_decisions.chosen: you bold man, most reckless of all
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both bold and the explicit superlative comparison with all (πάντων), not merely the intensifier utterly.

source_issues.issue: The nominal clause leaves its finite verbal relation implicit. The main text carries the preceding denial of doctrinal assertion forward; a direct nominal assertion, nor is the standing one going to stand as an adversary, is another grouping. Every surviving element remains.

passages.text: Peter said, “I will answer what you want, concerning ‘No one knew the Father except the Son, nor does anyone know the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.’ First, I am amazed how, when this statement has countless interpretations, you chose the more dangerous part, saying that the statement referred to ignorance on the part of the maker and everyone made by him. For in the first place the statement can have been addressed to all the Jews who supposed David to be the Messiah’s father—with the Messiah himself being the son—and had not recognized him as Son of God. Therefore it was appropriately said, ‘No one knew the Father,’ since everyone named David instead of God. He added, ‘Nor does anyone know the Son,’ because they did not know that he was Son. Saying, ‘Those to whom the Son wishes to reveal him,’ was also rightly said, for the Son who has existed from the beginning alone was appointed to reveal to those he wishes. Thus Adam, the first formed, can have been not ignorant of him; nor can Enoch, who pleased him, fail to know; nor can righteous Noah fail to understand; nor can Abraham the friend fail to comprehend; nor can Isaac have failed to understand; nor can Jacob who wrestled have failed to believe; nor can he have remained unrevealed to all the worthy among the people.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ ἐπικινδυνότερον ἐξελέξω μέρος
lexical_decisions.chosen: you chose the more dangerous part
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the comparative, not the unsupported superlative most dangerous.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πρὸς ἀγνωσίαν τοῦ δημιουργοῦ καὶ τῶν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ πάντων
lexical_decisions.chosen: ignorance on the part of the maker and everyone made by him
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitives are taken as subjective: maker and created ones are ignorant of the secret Father, as in Simon’s argument. Ignorance of the maker is an objective-genitive alternative, but fits the immediately preceding exchange less well.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῷ λαῷ ἀξίοις μὴ ἀποκεκαλύφθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: nor can he have remained unrevealed to all the worthy among the people
lexical_decisions.rationale: The final clause is read under the negative modal scope carried from the preceding οὐχ ... μὴ clauses. Its μὴ is retained in unrevealed and the carried denial in nor can. A clause-local reading, and not to have been revealed, remains possible but is less consonant with the preceding argument.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς πατέρα νομίζοντας εἶναι χριστοῦ τὸν Δαυὶδ — καὶ αὐτὸν δὲ τὸν χριστὸν υἱὸν ὄντα — καὶ υἱὸν θεοῦ μὴ ἐγνωκέναι.
lexical_decisions.chosen: who supposed David to be the Messiah’s father—with the Messiah himself being the son—and had not recognized him as Son of God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The printed parenthesis is kept outside the failure-to-recognize phrase and can continue the supposed Davidic father-son relation. It could instead affirm the Messiah’s sonship parenthetically. A broader attachment, taking their failure as not recognizing him as Son and as Son of God, is a material alternative, but the parenthetical punctuation favors keeping the explicit Son-of-God denial as the failed recognition.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐδὲ Ἐνὼχ ὁ εὐαρεστήσας μὴ εἰδέναι οὔτε Νῶε ὁ δίκαιος μὴ ἐπίστασθαι οὔτε Ἀβραὰμ ὁ φίλος μὴ συνιέναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: nor can Enoch ... fail to know; nor can righteous Noah fail to understand; nor can Abraham ... fail to comprehend
lexical_decisions.rationale: The governing δύναται is carried through the list, with οὐδέ/οὔτε denying the modal possibility of each negative-infinitive failure. This gives the explicit nor can ... fail construction. Another reading coordinates the negative infinitival complements under a positive possibility—can be not ignorant, can be not without knowledge—without the same emphasis on exclusion of ignorance. The first Adam clause has only the negative infinitive and is kept as a positive possibility of nonignorance; the later coordinated negatives are made explicit rather than flattened.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῷ λαῷ ἀξίοις μὴ ἀποκεκαλύφθαι
source_issues.issue: The final coordination has μὴ but no newly repeated οὐχ. The English carries the previous negative modal scope, nor can ... unrevealed, rather than adding a new printed negation. A clause-local reading would instead yield and not revealed. The modal/negative scope across the entire list is explained in the lexical note on Enoch, Noah, and Abraham.

passages.text: But if, as you say, he is to be revealed to everyone now through Jesus for the sake of knowing him, how do you not call it most unjust that those men did not know him—seven pillars of the world who were able to please the most just God—while now so many from the nations, impious in every way, know him? Were those men not deemed worthy to know the one better than all? And how is what is not just good? Unless by good you wish to mean not the one who benefits those who have acted justly, but the one who loves the unrighteous even if they do not believe, revealing to them also the secrets that he was unwilling to reveal to the righteous. Such conduct belongs neither to a good nor to a just being, but to one who hates the reverent. Are you perhaps the standing one, Simon, who is so emboldened as to say that these things were spoken in a way they never were?

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἑπτὰ στύλους ὑπάρξαντας κόσμῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: seven pillars of the world
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the stated seven without supplying an unprinted list of names.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μήτι σὺ εἶ, Σίμων, ὁ ἑστώς
lexical_decisions.chosen: Are you perhaps the standing one, Simon
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the standing epithet and interrogative challenge, not a translator’s identification of Simon.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ δὲ (ὡς φῄς) ἔσται διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ νῦν πᾶσιν ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι:
lexical_decisions.chosen: But if, as you say, he is to be revealed to everyone now through Jesus for the sake of knowing him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Is to be retains future ἔσται while now retains νῦν. The main text construes διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι purposively, for the sake of knowing, with him supplied as the contextual object, the previously discussed Father. The causal alternative is because of knowing; the clause does not state whose prior knowledge would ground disclosure on that attachment. No claim is added that the revealed one was already known to everyone.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὗτοι παντὸς κρείττονος γνῶναι οὐ κατηξιώθησαν;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Were those men not deemed worthy to know the one better than all?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context concerns knowing the proposed highest Father, favoring a personal referent superior to all and παντός as the comparison of κρείττονος. Taking παντός with substantival κρείττονος gives the broader alternative Were these not deemed worthy to know anything superior? The genitive superior object is construed with deemed worthy/knowing in this compressed phrase; the personal interpretation is not claimed as unique.

passages.text: Some sinned in this way from the supposition that, because of his goodness, he does not judge; others from the opposite view. For, supposing the statements of the scriptures against God to be true, although they are unjust and false, they did not know his true divinity and power. Therefore, supposing that he is ignorant, delights in murders, lets the wicked off through gifts of sacrifices, and also deceives, lies, and does everything unjust, they themselves, thinking they had acted like God, insisted while sinning that they were acting reverently. Therefore they were immovable toward what is better, and when admonished did not turn back. For they had no fear, considering themselves made like God through such actions.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰς γὰρ κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῶν γραφῶν φωνάς, ἀδίκους οὔσας καὶ ψευδεῖς
lexical_decisions.chosen: the statements of the scriptures against God ... although they are unjust and false
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the historical speaker’s explicit criticism of certain scriptural statements. It is neither softened nor presented as the translator’s own verdict about scripture.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκ ἐπεστρέφοντο
lexical_decisions.chosen: did not turn back
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the turning verb distinct from μετανοέω/reorient.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐκ τῆς διὰ τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἀκρίτου ὑπολήψεως
lexical_decisions.chosen: from the supposition that, because of his goodness, he does not judge
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text understands a supposition of God’s non-judging character, because 18.18 explicitly links presumed goodness with absence of pursuit of sins and judgment. Alternatively ἀκρίτου qualifies ὑπολήψεως: from the uncritical or unexamined supposition prompted by his goodness. On that attachment the adjective characterizes the supposition, not God’s judging activity. Neither reading is treated as a source defect.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αὐτοὶ ὡς ὅμοια θεοῦ ποιήσαντες, ἁμαρτάνοντες ἰσχυρίζοντο εὐσεβεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: they themselves, thinking they had acted like God, insisted while sinning that they were acting reverently
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὡς presents the alleged imitation from their viewpoint, not a fact affirmed by the narrator, who just called the accusations about God false. Had acted retains the retrospective aorist participle, while thinking makes their rationale explicit.

passages.text: As Simon said this and was about to go out, Peter said, “Hear this further thing from me, then go wherever you wish.” Simon turned and remained, and Peter said, “I know how you were astounded then when you heard me say, ‘Whoever says anything against the God who created the world, I do not believe him.’ Now hear something greater than this. If the God who created the world really were in character such as the scriptures describe him, and even if in some other way he were incomparably evil, beyond what either the scriptures could say or anyone else could even conceive, I would nevertheless not stop revering him alone and doing his will. For I want you to know and be persuaded that the person who has no affection for his own maker can never have it for another either. If he does have it for another, he has it contrary to nature and does not know that he has from evil the love of the unjust, since he cannot even keep that love firm. And if there really is someone else above the maker, being good he will receive me all the more because I love my own Father; but he will not receive you, knowing that you abandoned your maker by nature—I do not say father—for a greater hope, without concern for what is reasonable. Thus, if you find someone superior even to him, he knows that you will abandon him too someday, especially since he has not become your father, when you have abandoned even your true father.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐὰν τῷ ὄντι ὁ τὸν κόσμον κτίσας θεὸς τὴν γνώμην τοιοῦτος ὢν τυγχάνῃ
lexical_decisions.chosen: If the God who created the world really were in character such as ...
lexical_decisions.rationale: The description is explicitly hypothetical. The severe conditional is preserved, not rewritten as an assertion that the maker is evil.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐκ πονηροῦ τὸν τῶν ἀδίκων ἔρωτα ἔχων
lexical_decisions.chosen: he has from evil the love of the unjust
lexical_decisions.rationale: From evil adopts the impersonal reading of πονηροῦ, since the immediate context does not identify a personal evil agent. From an evil one or the evil one is grammatically possible but is not asserted through imported theology. Love of the unjust may be love characteristic of unjust people or love directed toward them; the main phrase retains that ambiguity.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν φύσει σου ποιητὴν (οὐ γὰρ λέγω πατέρα)
lexical_decisions.chosen: your maker by nature—I do not say father
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Peter’s pointed change from father to maker in addressing Simon rather than harmonizing all parent-language.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὕτως εἰ καὶ αὐτοῦ κρείττονα εὑρήσεις
lexical_decisions.chosen: Thus, if you find someone superior even to him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Superior retains broader comparative κρείττονα without specifying the basis of superiority. Better or stronger are material alternatives, but the argument about changing allegiances does not require strength alone.
